name: Default model download integrity check
answer:
YES TO BOTH, AND THE RUNTIME DOWNLOAD GOES AWAY ENTIRELY. The question was whether checkpoints should be checksum-verified and partial downloads discarded.

WHAT LEGACY DOES. Without a custom model it looks for sam_vit_h_4b8939.pth, moves it from ~/.cache/lazylabel if it is there, and otherwise fetches it from dl.fbaipublicfiles.com in 1 KiB chunks with a 30 second timeout. The only integrity check is that the number of bytes received equals Content-Length. That check sees exactly one failure - a download cut short - and is blind to every other: corruption on disk, a half-written file from a previous run, a mirror serving something else, a file edited after it arrived.

And it does not even catch the one thing it is for. The card records that a network error leaves the partial file in place, because only the generic error branch deletes it. So the next start finds a file of the right name, skips the download, and fails to load a truncated checkpoint. The user sees a model-loading error with no indication that the cause is a 1.2 GB fragment sitting on their disk, and retrying does not help, because the retry is what is being skipped. A caching scheme whose failure mode is a permanent one is worse than no caching.

ANSWER, and it is stronger than the question asked for. Checksum-verified: every checkpoint is pinned by SHA-256 in a manifest, and one that does not match is refused with the expected and actual digests named. Partial downloads discarded: there are no downloads. Nothing is fetched at runtime at all (SEC-03, SEC-05, SEC-17) - the build pipeline mirrors checkpoints to disk and the manifest describes what should be there. A service that never downloads cannot leave a fragment behind, which is a better answer than remembering to delete one.

BUILT IN PHASE 2, at `inference/src/lazylabel_inference/manifest.py`. `check_checkpoint` compares the byte count first because it is free and catches precisely the truncated-file case with a message that names it - 'a partial download left in place is the usual cause' - and then hashes in 1 MiB chunks, because a SAM checkpoint is gigabytes and reading one whole to hash it would cost as much memory as the model. The result is a status, not an exception: present, verified, and a detail string, so `/health` and `/models` can report a broken checkpoint as a configuration fault rather than a crash. Tested at `tests/test_manifest.py`, including the right-size-wrong-bytes case that Content-Length cannot see at all.

FOR PHASE 3, one thing this does not yet cover: the load itself must use weights-only loading, so that a checkpoint which passes its hash is still not an arbitrary-code-execution path if the manifest is ever wrong. Hash verification and weights-only loading are different defences against different mistakes, and Phase 3's exit criterion 3 requires both.
corrections: Recorded that legacy's Content-Length check does not catch its own target case, because the partial file survives the network error and the next start skips the download rather than retrying it.
Strengthened the answer beyond 'discard partial downloads' to 'do not download at runtime', which makes the partial-file case unreachable rather than handled.
Noted that hash verification does not replace weights-only loading; Phase 3 exit criterion 3 needs both.
